Chapter IV

The Incorporation and Expansion of the College, 1880-1890

INCORPORATION AND CHARACTERIZATION

INCORPORATION.—By 1880 the Halsel-Holland school had grown to such importance and the tracking of the students was so well appreciated that formalities could be expected. The 1880 catalog gives 1879 as the date of incorporation; the actual charter, as recorded in the state legislature. The charter, which was granted on January 22, 1880. The incorporators were James Paxton, J. B. Chenoweth, R. J. Abernathy, R. B. Halsel, and Lewis Holland, of whose photographs and biographical sketches appear in Chapter VI. The charter was filed in the Department of State February 14, 1880. It stipulated that the institution shall be called SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE; that the purpose for which it was established was "to maintain a School or Seminary of Learning for the education of Males and Females in the useful and ornamental branches of education; to employ the Faculty of said school to confer the degrees of Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science, and such other degrees of Proficiency, and to Issue such Diplomas as the Institution shall be entitled to grant;" and that the charter should be for a period of fifty years; that the number of trustees should not be less than five and not more than fifteen (five are named); and that they should have power to elect their successors or to fill vacancies within the said time; should reside in Fannin County; and that the amount of capital stock of the corporation was not less than $1,500, in shares of two hundred and fifty.
